title: Best Time to Buy a Grill: Why Fall Wins
dek: Grills are on sale somewhere every month, but the good prices come after the grilling season, not before it. Here is the calendar and what to do if you can't wait.
author: viewdeals-desk
meta_description: Grill prices fall after the Fourth of July and again from Labor Day into fall. A month-by-month guide to when to buy, with sources and a checklist.

sections.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: Buy a grill when other people have stopped wanting one. Both sources we read say the best prices come in late summer and fall, once the grilling season is winding down, and that the busy weeks before summer are the weakest time to look for a real discount.

Clark.com, whose guide was updated in June 2026, says its deals team has seen the best grill prices in early fall in recent years and expects the lowest prices in September. DealNews, which counts the grill deals it lists each month, describes the same pattern in more detail.

paragraphs: The table follows DealNews's account of the year. Its figures come from its own deal listings in earlier years, so they show when deals were posted, not what every store charged.

sections.heading: Why spring and early summer disappoint
paragraphs: It seems natural to shop for a grill around Memorial Day or Father's Day, and there are sales then. DealNews says those discounts are often not noteworthy, and that the good ones tend to cover a small selection. Its own counts make the point: May and June had the most grill deals of any months, about a sixth of the year's total each, yet January and November had more of the deals its editors rated as the best.
Clark.com puts it more bluntly: buy at the height of the season and you will probably pay full price.

sections.heading: Why fall is better
paragraphs: After the Fourth of July, DealNews says, demand begins to fall and the offers get better than anything in May or June. Labor Day weekend then starts a longer run of sales, because by that point almost nobody is shopping for a grill and stores want the floor space.

Clark.com adds that prices keep moving after Labor Day as grills become clearance stock, and advises comparing prices and buying quickly when a good one appears, because clearance stock does not come back.

sections.heading: Where to look
paragraphs: Clark.com's record of the grill deals it has posted since 2016 has Walmart as a frequent source, and it also points to the seasonal sales at Home Depot and Lowe's. Money expert Clark Howard, the site notes, often shops at smaller discount stores as well. We list grill deals from Walmart, Target and Best Buy when they pass our checks; the big home-improvement stores are worth checking yourself.

sections.heading: If you can't wait until fall
paragraphs: A grill bought in September is not much use for a July cookout. If you need one for summer, DealNews's advice is that saving something is better than saving nothing: deals exist every month, just with less choice. Buying a little after the Fourth of July, not before it, is the easy compromise, since the offers improve and most of the summer is still ahead.

sections.heading: What to check before you buy
paragraphs: Check the size and the fuel. A discount on a grill that is too small for your household, or that uses a fuel you would rather not deal with, is not a saving.
Check what is included. Covers, side shelves and propane tanks are often sold separately, and assembly and delivery can be extra.
Compare prices on the day. Clark.com suggests a comparison tool such as Google Shopping and a price-history site, so that you can see whether today's price is really low for that model.

sections.heading: How we will keep this guide honest
paragraphs: ViewDeals began recording prices at Walmart, Target and Best Buy on November 26, 2026. That record is too short to say anything about a full year yet, so this guide rests on the sources named. When our own checks can add to it, we will put them here and say how many checks they are based on.
